Triggers.value: Feeling physically restrained or held down

Memory.value: Something in my surroundings can instantly bring back the full memory without warning
When the memory returns I feel so overwhelmed by emotion that I have to stop
My memories of the frightening event are very clear and detailed.

vignette: Kien, a 76-year-old Vietnamese man, had lived through unimaginable horrors during the war. As a civilian in a war-torn city, he witnessed and experienced atrocities that would haunt him for decades to come. One particular incident stood out - the day he was caught by enemy soldiers and physically restrained while his family was taken away. The feeling of being held down, unable to move or protect those he loved, left an indelible mark on Kien's psyche. Years later, as a warehouse worker in the United States, Kien found himself constantly on edge. Confrontations with coworkers would send his heart racing, transporting him back to that fateful day. The slightest whiff of diesel fuel or smoke would instantly bring back the memories - the smell was always the first trigger, followed by an overwhelming sense of panic and dread. When this happened, Kien's mind would flood with vivid images of the war-torn streets, the sounds of gunfire and screams, and the feeling of being utterly helpless. These unannounced visits from his past left Kien breathless and disoriented. He'd have to stop whatever he was doing, unable to shake off the emotions that came crashing down on him like a tidal wave. His memories were so clear and detailed that it felt as though no time had passed at all - he could still smell the sweat and fear on his skin, taste the metallic tang of blood in his mouth. These episodes would leave Kien reeling for hours, making it impossible for him to concentrate or interact with others. As a result, Kien began to avoid confrontations at work, sidestepping any situation that might lead to conflict. He'd take long detours on his way home, avoiding streets where he knew the smell of diesel fuel lingered in the air. His coworkers noticed the change in him, but Kien couldn't explain it - even to himself. All he knew was that those memories had a hold on him, and he didn't know how to break free. Lately, however, these avoidance tactics were no longer enough. The memories continued to resurface, triggered by something as innocuous as the smell of cooking oil or the sound of sirens in the distance. It was as though his mind had become a minefield, waiting for the slightest misstep to unleash the horrors he thought he'd left behind. Kien knew then that it was time to seek help - not just for himself, but for those around him who deserved better than a shell of a man haunted by his past. As he sat in his dimly lit living room, surrounded by mementos from a life well-lived, Kien felt the weight of his memories bearing down on him. He knew that seeking help would mean confronting these demons head-on - something he'd been trying to avoid for decades. Yet, with every passing day, the thought of being trapped in this never-ending cycle became more unbearable than the prospect of facing what he feared most: reliving the war all over again.
